definition: Eurotra was a machine translation project established and funded by the European Commission from 1978 until 1992.
details: Eurotra was a machine translation project established and funded by the European Commission from 1978 until 1992.

explainer.lead: Eurotra was a European Commission project devoted to machine translation, established in 1978 and funded until 1992. It represents a sustained institutional effort to develop automatic translation rather than a single algorithm or software release.

tiers.eli5: Like a long, government-funded team project to build a translator that could work across many European languages.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers today encounter Eurotra mainly as historical context in machine translation research rather than as a component to build on; the project ended in 1992, so its methods are not a current toolkit.
tiers.paperLevel: It is defined only as a European Commission machine translation project spanning 1978 to 1992; no formal definition or performance bounds are specified.

explainer.example: Consider a document that needs to be translated by a computer rather than entirely by a person. Building that kind of automatic translation capability was the general aim of the Eurotra project.
explainer.intuition: The idea was to pursue automatic translation through a shared, long-term European project. Its defining features are its machine translation goal, its European Commission backing, and its 1978–1992 duration.
howItWorks: The European Commission established Eurotra in 1978.
The project focused on machine translation: using computers to translate between languages.
The Commission funded the effort through 1992.
explainer.whyItMatters: Eurotra is a notable historical example of a machine translation effort sustained by a public institution over many years. Its 1978 start also places it well before many of today's widely used translation systems.
misconceptions: Eurotra was a project, not simply the name of one algorithm.
1992 marks the end of the stated funding period, not the project's beginning.
Its broad machine translation goal does not by itself identify a particular technical method.
